correctness.rationale: Every column cut has an even number of graph vertices on the left and two crossing edges, so a perfect matching uses both crossing edges or neither. This gives exactly the claimed monomer/dimer tilings. An endpoint fault forces one horizontal pair. For an interior fault the two ways to cover column j each give a cone on the corresponding forced pair. Common faces contain no edge incident to columns j-1,j,j+1. Their restrictions are extendible in the remaining subladders: each occupied horizontal tile is disjoint from the others because the face already extends in the full graph, and all unused columns in a subladder can take rungs. Conversely a pair of such restricted faces can be completed with either forced pair and the rung on the third deleted-from-overlap column. Thus the intersection is the exact join. Simplicial inclusions are cofibrations, so the nonempty intersection suspends up to homotopy. When both factors are L_0, the only interior case is n=3,j=2 and the two cones are disjoint, giving S^0. The intact classification can also be checked directly: split at the first column into the rung and paired-horizontal cones. Their intersection consists of extendible faces on the last m-2 columns, since the rung branch can fill column 2 with its rung. Thus for m>=3 the intact type suspends the type at m-2; the bases at m=1 and m=2 are a point and two disjoint simplices. The two overlap lengths add to n-3; they are both even exactly when n is odd and j is even, with zero lengths omitted as join identities. The join is then a sphere of dimension (n-5)/2 except in the already treated empty case, and suspension gives (n-3)/2. Otherwise a positive odd length gives a contractible join and union.
residual_risks: The bounded backtracking validates 44 structural cases, not homology or arbitrary n. The source's replay path is python verify_rung_fault.py; its stated mod-two computation was not independently rerun. The homotopy classification is justified by the proof, not extrapolated from mod-two ranks.

value.rationale: This is a complete positional topology classification for one natural graph defect: in an otherwise contractible odd straight ladder, one local fault can create a sphere whose dimension grows without bound, but only at alternate positions. The exact product-like simplicial join explains the two boundary distances controlling the effect and can be used independently of the homotopy conclusion. Neither an endpoint calculation nor intact homology alone captures this mechanism.
residual_risks: The value concerns one vertical fault and ordinary homotopy type; it does not establish simultaneous or horizontal-fault laws, simple homotopy or equivariant conclusions.
